D.D-PHASE-1: Build 23.4's milestones straight through in dependency order, staffed as 23.5 proposes; each recURd stage releases once whole.
D.D-PHASE-2: No code before G0, signed 2026-11-06; an unsettled blocker defers what it blocks; implementation findings return as Q- items.
D.D-TEAM-30: Delegations admit exact tags with a not_after floor and max_admits for life, ending at DelegationRevoke, void or compromise.
D.D-TEAM-31: Revoking or suspending a tagged agent shows the agent, its Delegation's shared key and admission authority apart.
D.D-TEAM-32: Revocations, suspensions, vetoes, admissions, AdminSet changes, member removals, recovery bindings and presence-key changes carry the signer's live presence key's countersignature.
D.D-KEYS-24: ReaderWraps and DelegationWraps are typed KeyDeliveries naming the recipient key; late ones carry their signer's AuthPin and time.
D.D-KEYS-25: ReaderKeys live 7 days, replaced at 6, so passive keychain copies heal in about 37 days; active clones need revocation.
D.D-KEYS-26: gkm routes take 10.6's scopes; read_only devices keep their own ReaderKeys, KeyPackages, reads, acks and commits under r.
D.D-MCP-33: Team-directory erasure takes admin; a repo owner's revocation files an erasure request that the directory's erasure runner completes.
D.D-MCP-34: Directory approvals and denials complete by one resumable protocol, rewriting the notice with DecisionRefs that requesters read directly.
D.D-MCP-35: A repo item counts only if its signer's right holds at its push's pin, judged from retained history.
D.D-EVS-66: An erasure's first index push, a CUT, moves the head's index_epoch; other index pushes name it and apply the set.
D.D-EVS-67: An erasure's wait is stated from its rekey objects and allowance; its CUT and first ERASE land at once.
D.D-OPS-22: Until the move tool, a cluster at 80% raw or 70% inodes refuses payload 507 CLUSTER_FULL; exhaustion projected per cluster.
D.D-SDK-31: CheckSend and GetSendResult give each recipient domain's DATA cap, predicted outcome and result; receiver coverage speaks only of receiving.
D.D-PROTO-22: A marked pair's reports are withheld to each 55-minute window's end and fixed at a 256 KiB floor a direction.
D.D-EVS-23: A push id names one statement; retries return its version; the head resolves unknown outcomes and records unsettled refusals.
D.D-EVS-33: One write budget per metadata cluster (0.8 DWPD, 50% IOPS) except P0; P1 prepays P2 by wallet; heaviest refused first.
D.D-OPS-20: Both clusters run an in-house `urnetwork/minio` build whose drive commits apply only before deadlines and release keys once settled.
D.D-KEYS-16: KeyHolders: leaves, uncovered agents, live Delegations, recovery keys; a Delegation's key drops at revocation, not_after, Suspend or non-reap revocation.
D.D-EVS-52: Only a document's newest version yields hits, probed per candidate in a bounded version table, tombstones and erasure sets included.
D.D-CORE-20: Approval-capable devices revoke their member's other devices as `lost` or `compromise`, countersigned by their presence key where registered, else confirmed.
D.D-MCP-8: run_restore writes only the run's attributed edits, checked on the bytes it moves aside, recorded, approved when tainted.
D.D-EVS-41: git-lfs uses versionless `ur/lfs`; tips commit only with their objects protected; prunes drop what no tip or recent commit needs.
D.D-SDK-27: At foreground, apps Hello their first-choice own indexer, then Ping it each minute; failover waits 3 s (5 s metered).
D.D-TLS-12: Active custom hosts reach tlsedge via a versioned map, each ready once every serving interface's reported version passes route probes.
D.D-SDK-16: Wakes follow 18.7: a slot-local script ordering token projections by revision, a separate enqueue, frame acks, a deferred live check.
D.D-MAIL-14: Receivers seal bounded reception-time authentication evidence in the deposit; readers label, score and forward from it, never from later DNS.
D.D-TEST-10: Every state machine of §7-§21 is tested by deterministic fault schedules against FI-1 to FI-30, beside TLA+ and Porcupine checks.
D.D-EVS-12: 11.6-11.7's token tree, re-keyed at once on removal or compromise, else within 24 h or, deferred, once a source drops.
D.D-TEST-17: FS-86 gates the directory against 16.11's cost table: its M6 case at M6's Gn-out, its card case later.

Q-EVS-24: Must the PM9A3 write bound hold against aggregate P0 safety work?
(b), owner decisions 186, 190: P0 runs at once, outside the wear bound, alarmed.
Q-PROTO-4: Should connect keep remote search's byte totals per contract, which show roughly how many search pages ran in each contract hour?
(b), owner decisions 176, 188, 191: marked pairs report windows at a 256 KiB floor.
